$note: Golden vectors for `[editor].attachment_folder` — where a dropped or pasted image lands. This is a CROSS-LANGUAGE CONTRACT, and it exists because the placement rule is now implemented twice: Rust owns the real placement (`attachment_dir_for_page` in the desktop app's editor attachments module, read at store time) and TypeScript owns the Site-settings preview line (`attachmentDirForPage` in the frontend's attachment-placement settings, recomputed on every keystroke). A preview that disagreed with the placement would be worse than no preview at all, so both sides read THIS FILE directly — there is no generated copy, so the two cannot drift.
$encoding: One stored string, three meanings: "" = next to the page; "./NAME" = subfolder of the page's own folder; "NAME" = folder relative to the site root.

placement.note: page at the site root -> the root
page at the root: the subfolder IS a root folder
nested page keeps its whole folder
bare value is site-wide, page location irrelevant
same folder from a root page

$validation_note: `error` is null when the value is accepted, else the KIND of rejection: "absolute" (a path that would escape the site — leading slash, leading backslash, or a Windows drive prefix, checked on every platform because config.toml travels) or "dotdot" (any `..` component, split on both slash flavours).

validation.note: leading dots are only a problem as a whole component

$exclusion_note: The inverse question, asked by the build: is this scanned directory attachment storage rather than a section of the site? Storage gets no index page, no listing row, no nav entry. `dir` is a project-relative directory path; `excluded` is the answer. Only Rust reads this array — the Site-settings preview shows placement, not exclusion — but the encoding stays defined in ONE file so the two questions cannot drift apart.

exclusion.note: default: attachments sit beside the page, so no folder is storage
bare value: exactly this root folder
bare value is root-anchored: a same-named folder elsewhere is content
prefix match must stop at a segment boundary
the parent of a storage folder is still content
a root-level page's own folder IS the root, so root assets/ is storage
the site root is never storage
